jessica: Heads-up — PR <https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1876|runtime#1876> is ready but I'm pausing merge until we get an arch check on the KV-cache routing changes. RFC linked: https://docs.internal.redwood/rfcs/kv-routing-2026.
raja: Thanks — can you summarize the risk? quick bullets please.
jessica: Short: new shard-selection heuristic can change request affinity. Risk = increased tail latency for some long-context workloads if fallback isn't configured. Also requires a small config change to the autoscaler to avoid hot-shard overload.
kevin: @jessica can you paste the exact config diff? I want to check autoscaler knobs.
jessica: Sure, here's the snippet:
```
autoscaler:
  shard_hot_threshold: 0.85 -> 0.9
  fallback_policy: prefer-siblings
```
jessica: Also added a safe fallback that routes to a compatible model-variant when hot shard detected.
raja: OK. @kevin can you give an architecture ack or list required mitigations? we need to decide whether we can merge before EOD.
kevin: I'll look in 15m. Initial thought: need a canary with 10% traffic -> 0.85 threshold, and metrics alert on per-shard queue depth + p99 latency. Add a temporary rollout flag so we can flip back quickly. If tests pass and metrics look good after 30m, approve.
jessica: I'll add the canary plan to the PR description and add the rollout flag. Will also attach a test prompt set for long-context perf.
ci-bot: deploy-bot: canary job scheduled: runtime/canary/kv-routing-1876 -> 10% region-eu-west1, 30m window.
raja: Great. @kevin please drop a short ack here when you're happy so I can merge after the canary window.
kevin: Ack from arch assuming canary metrics are green and alert thresholds are added. :white_check_mark:
jessica: Thanks both — updating PR now with rollout steps + exact alerts. Will ping when canary finishes.
raja: Perfect, thanks.
